course_name_en: Metals: Phase Equilibria, Solidification and Heat Treatments
prerequisites: Basic knowledge of materials science as taught in the course "Introduction to Materials Science" (H01D0A)

learning_outcomes.text: To establish the relationship between the structure and microstructure of materials and their properties.
To apply this relationship intensively in designing materials for specific properties and applications.
To tailor materials using specific material treatments that influence structure and microstructure.

syllabus_topics: Paradigms for alloy development based on microstructure design
Basic concepts of equilibrium thermodynamics for pure systems
Derivation and interpretation of binary phase diagrams
Application: Diffusion and growth of intermetallic phases in soldering
Growth of the solid phase in pure metals
Growth of a single solid phase in alloys
Solid-Solid phase transformations and heat treatments
Homogeneous and heterogeneous nucleation in solid-solid phase transformations
Thermally activated growth mechanisms in solid-solid transformations
Setting up and interpreting TTT and CCT diagrams
assessment_rules: To participate in the evaluation during the examination period, attendance at all laboratory sessions and passing the pass/fail test after the last lab session are required. The evaluation characteristics and determination of the final result for the second examination opportunity are identical to those of the first examination opportunity.
bibliography: Accompanying bundle and addendum with useful diagrams and a description of the microstructures for the lab sessions on Toledo
institution: KU Leuven - Faculty of Engineering Science
degree: Bachelor in de ingenieurswetenschappen (Bachelor of Engineering Science, Leuven)
